assembly_findings: After calling 0x140d4a810 with this+0x10, the provider builds +0x48 + '://' + +0x58.

When +0x68 is nonempty, 0x141c40bb8 calls 0x142bace90 on it with '/' (0x145a95874), search parameters 0, 0, -1. If the result equals -1, 0x140a46a63 constructs '/' followed by the entire component; otherwise 0x14900e06f copies the component. This is a search for a slash anywhere, not a leading-slash test.
When +0x78 is nonempty, 0x140a46beb branches to append '/' and then the whole +0x78 component, regardless of its contents. Empty components add nothing.

The provider's 0x140a46d43 return path restores saved registers and returns the output address; no matching release call appears in that path. Its input components are copied into temporary/output FStrings.
validation: Bounded static instruction traces, literal inspection and comparison to local UE SSL interface and Windows platform implementation; no build or runtime tests.

initial_callee_contract.ssl_access: 0x1438bce20 is FSslModule::Get: it caches a module pointer, or loads the module named SSL. At 0x14905aa3e the returned module+0x10 is the certificate manager; vtable+0x28 is ISslCertificateManager::IsDomainPinned, as corroborated by the engine interface. It receives &service+0x58. It is called even when the protocol will fail.
initial_callee_contract.protocol: Case-insensitive comparison against https then, only if different, wss. 0x142bcf780 performs the case-insensitive TCHAR comparison. bBadProtocol is true exactly if both compare unequal; bBadDomain is the negated result of IsDomainPinned.
initial_callee_contract.failure: If either boolean is true, conditionally emits severity-2 MCP logging containing Exiting due to OSS connection attempt to unpinned protocol (%d %s) or domain (%d %s), with bBadProtocol, scheme, bBadDomain, host in that order. It then calls 0x142ce8ac0(false), independent of log suppression. The latter contains the literal FPlatformMisc::RequestExit(%i), the reason Win RequestExit, termination delegate, and non-force PostQuitMessage path, identifying FWindowsPlatformMisc::RequestExit(false). The exit request may return; the provider continues constructing its result.
initial_callee_contract.object_effects: No direct writes to service fields or lock acquisition/release occur in the traced callee. SSL module load, the certificate-manager virtual call, error logging and exit request are externally visible effects; callers cannot replace the gate by plain string assembly or assume a deployment host.
initial_callee_contract.limitations: Category identity/logging plumbing and downstream virtual implementation are not reconstructed here. A faithful source lift needs the actual SSL module dependency and MCP log category (or an explicit equivalent integration), and must retain the gate and exit request. No .inc or manifest claims complete recovery.
